title: 2014 HMMT February Geometry Problem 6
statement: In quadrilateral \(A B C D\), we have \(A B=5, B C=6, C D=5, D A=4\), and \(\angle A B C=90^{\circ}\). Let \(A C\) and \(B D\) meet at \(E\). Compute \(\frac{B E}{E D}\).

solutions.text: \(\sqrt{3}\) We find that \(A C=\sqrt{61}\), and applying the law of cosines to triangle \(A C D\) tells us that \(\angle A D C=120\). Then \(\frac{B E}{E D}\) is the ratio of the areas of triangles \(A B C\) and \(A D C\), which is \(\frac{(5)(6)}{(4)(5) \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}=\sqrt{3}\).
